llm.text: Doctors determine if someone has asthma by taking a medical history and asking about symptoms such as coughing, especially at night, wheezing, chest tightness, triggers like exercise or seasonal changes, and family history of asthma or allergies [P1]. They also perform a physical exam and may use lung‑function tests, most commonly spirometry, which measures how much air you can exhale before and after using asthma medication [P1][P2]. Additional tests can include peak expiratory flow measurements, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) testing to assess airway inflammation, and allergy skin or blood tests to identify specific triggers [P2][P4]. If needed, specialists such as an asthma or allergy doctor may be consulted for further evaluation [P3].
